relationships.description: Connects Floyd-Warshall All-Pairs Shortest Paths to core algorithm patterns in the broader engineering catalog.

concept.tagline: A dynamic-programming algorithm that computes shortest paths between all pairs of vertices in O(V³) time and O(V²) space, detecting negative cycles.
concept.purpose: Build a progressive mental model of Floyd-Warshall—from why intermediate vertex k must be the outermost loop to INF+INF overflow guards and FX arbitrage detection.

spark.summary: A dynamic-programming algorithm that computes shortest paths between all pairs of vertices in O(V^3) time and O(V^2) space, handling negative edge weights and detecting negative cycles.
spark.keyTakeaway: With just three nested loops (`k` outermost), Floyd-Warshall solves all-pairs shortest paths and negative-cycle detection on dense graphs up to V ≈ 500 in milliseconds.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** Floyd-Warshall computes the shortest path between **every** pair `(i, j)` in a weighted directed or undirected graph using the dynamic-programming recurrence: `dist[i][j] = min(dist[i][j], dist[i][k] + dist[k][j])` At step `k`.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Floyd-Warshall Intermediate Vertex Relaxation (k Outermost) (BASE MATRIX (k=-1) -> RELAX VIA k (0..V-1) -> NEG CYCLE DETECTED); Lock-Free Double-Buffered All-Pairs Matrix Swap (PoP Telemetry -> FW Builder Thread -> Atomic Matrix Ptr -> Routing Readers).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Pick the all-pairs algorithm based on graph density and whether negative weights exist. Because Floyd-Warshall mutates `dist[i][j]` in-place across `k` iterations, serving routers must never read the matrix mid-computation.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Compare Floyd-Warshall with single-source and MST graph algorithms.

learningJourney.title: What is Floyd-Warshall
learningJourney.explanation:
Floyd-Warshall computes the shortest path between **every** pair `(i, j)` in a weighted directed or undirected graph using the dynamic-programming recurrence:

`dist[i][j] = min(dist[i][j], dist[i][k] + dist[k][j])`

At step `k`, `dist[i][j]` holds the shortest path from `i` to `j` using only intermediate vertices from `{0, ..., k}`. Crucially, `k` **must** be the outermost loop so all `k-1` subpaths are finalized before being combined. If any diagonal entry ends with `dist[i][i] < 0`, the graph contains a **negative-weight cycle**.

sectionDiagram.title: Floyd-Warshall Intermediate Vertex Relaxation (k Outermost)
sectionDiagram.summary: Iterating k outermost lets the 3D DP table collapse to a single V x V matrix updated in-place.

learningJourney.purpose: The mechanism: understand how Floyd-Warshall works from first principles.

learningJourney.title: Why Real Systems Need All-Pairs Matrices & Negative-Cycle Checks
learningJourney.explanation: Single-source algorithms like Dijkstra cannot handle negative edge weights and waste setup overhead on small dense meshes. Cloud PoP latency tables (`V ≈ 180` in a near-complete mesh) and FX currency arbitrage (`-ln(rate)` edges) need an all-to-all matrix where `180³ = 5.83M` tight loop ops run in `<4 ms` inside L2 cache.

ideas.title: INF + INF Overflow Trap
ideas.description: Always guard `if dist[i][k] == INF or dist[k][j] == INF: continue` before adding, or `INT_MAX + INT_MAX` wraps negative.

ideas.title: Path Reconstruction via `next[i][j]`
ideas.description: Store `next[i][j] = next[i][k]` strictly on `<` (not `<=`) to reconstruct any shortest path in `O(path_len)`.

learningJourney.purpose: The problem: see what breaks without Why Real Systems Need All-Pairs Matrices & Negative-Cycle Checks under real concurrency or scale.

learningJourney.title: Where Floyd-Warshall Fits (and Where It Hits a Wall)
learningJourney.explanation: Cubic `O(V³)` scaling is blazingly fast up to `V ≈ 500`, then hits a wall (`V = 2,000` is `8 × 10⁹` ops).

benefits: Auto-vectorized flat `V x V` array loops beat `V` runs of heap-based Dijkstra in constant factors.
costs: In-place updates require double-buffering if serving lock-free concurrent reads.

comparison.choice: Good Candidate: FX Arbitrage & Transitive Closure
benefits: Detects negative cycles (`dist[c][c] < -1e-9`) across `-ln(rate)` edges in microseconds.
costs: Must clamp negative-cycle cascading to `-INF` if continuing past detection.

comparison.choice: Avoid: Large Sparse Graphs (V > 1,000, E = O(V))
benefits: `V` runs of Dijkstra (`O(V E log V)`) or Johnson's algorithm (`O(V² log V + V E)`) run 100x–1,000x faster.
costs: Floyd-Warshall wastes `O(V³)` iterations on missing edges.

learningJourney.purpose: Scope boundary: identify where this pattern fits best and where simpler or async alternatives win.

learningJourney.title: Safe k-i-j Loop, Overflow Guard & Negative-Cycle Detection
learningJourney.explanation: Keep `k` outermost, guard `INF` additions, and inspect the diagonal after completion.
learningJourney.purpose: Operational control: configure bounds, failure handling, and safe production defaults.

learningJourney.title: Alternatives: Floyd-Warshall vs. Johnson's vs. Repeated Dijkstra
learningJourney.explanation: Pick the all-pairs algorithm based on graph density and whether negative weights exist.

benefits: Handles negative weights, 3 nested loops, zero heap allocations, fits `V <= 512` in L2/L3 cache.
costs: Unusable for `V > 1,500` due to cubic scaling.

benefits: Reweights negative edges via 1 Bellman-Ford pass, then runs `V` fast Dijkstras on sparse graphs.
costs: Higher implementation complexity and heap overhead on dense graphs.

benefits: Ideal for sparse road/network graphs with non-negative latencies.
costs: Fails silently on negative edge weights.

learningJourney.purpose: The trade-off: compare competing approaches across latency, consistency, and operational cost.

learningJourney.title: Production SDN Routing: Double-Buffered Matrix Publishing
learningJourney.explanation: Because Floyd-Warshall mutates `dist[i][j]` in-place across `k` iterations, serving routers must never read the matrix mid-computation. Production controllers compute the new matrix on a background buffer and atomically swap a read-only pointer.

sectionDiagram.title: Lock-Free Double-Buffered All-Pairs Matrix Swap
sectionDiagram.summary: Double-buffering isolates in-place O(V³) DP mutations from concurrent low-latency route lookups.

_recommendedProblem.title: Active-Active Multi-Master Split-Brain Recovery
_recommendedProblem.prompt: Redesign an active-active multi-master relational replication pipeline between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 (6,000 writes/sec, 85 ms WAN RTT, < 15 ms p99 local commit) so a 9-minute transatlantic partition and 180-250 ms NTP clock skew never cause silent Last-Write-Wins (LWW) overwrites.
